title: Do corporate caterers in Dubai provide invoices for expenses?
body_markdown:
Yes—ask your Dubai corporate caterer to issue an invoice in your company’s legal name and confirm the required details before booking. For a corporate catering invoice in Dubai, expense approval and VAT recovery are separate checks: your finance team decides what supports reimbursement, while VAT treatment depends on the supplier, the document and the purpose of the expense.


**TL;DR**

- A corporate catering invoice in Dubai should identify the supplier, your company, the event and the charges.
- The UAE Federal Tax Authority distinguishes a tax invoice from a quotation or payment receipt.
- A valid tax invoice does not automatically make catering VAT recoverable.
- Confirm company details, purchase-order references and invoice requirements before approving the booking.


## Do corporate caterers in Dubai provide invoices for expenses?

**Request an invoice before confirming the event, rather than assuming a booking message or card receipt will satisfy finance.** Ask the caterer whether it can issue the document your organisation requires, including a tax invoice where applicable.

For supplier selection, the guide to [corporate event catering companies in Dubai](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/best-corporate-event-catering-companies-in-dubai) is a related starting point. Treat invoice requirements as a separate procurement check alongside the menu, service format and practical arrangements.

Different documents serve different purposes. Keeping them separate helps you avoid submitting a quotation as evidence of a completed purchase.

| Document | Best for | What it establishes | Limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quotation | Approving the proposed scope | Proposed menu, service and charges | Does not establish that payment or delivery occurred |
| Pro forma invoice | Arranging advance payment | A request for payment against proposed arrangements | Is not a tax invoice |
| Invoice or tax invoice, as applicable | Recording the supplier’s charge | The billed service and relevant financial details | Does not necessarily prove payment |
| Receipt or payment confirmation | Supporting payment reconciliation | Evidence that a payment was made | Does not automatically replace a tax invoice |

Ask finance which documents it needs for the specific route: a company purchase, an employee reimbursement or a supplier payment. Those routes can require different supporting records.

## Why the paperwork matters before you book

An invoice needs to connect the catering charge to the company that authorised it. If the booking uses an employee’s name but the expense belongs to a business, resolve the billing details before the supplier prepares the document.

**Confirm the billed entity before confirming the menu.** This is particularly useful when your organisation has several companies, branches or departments and the event organiser is not the person approving payment.

For myCHEF corporate catering enquiries, include the business event requirements and the billing requirements in the same brief. Ask for confirmation of the documentation before making a booking decision; do not assume a particular invoicing workflow from the service description alone.

## What should you request on a corporate catering invoice?

Give the supplier accurate company information and ask finance to check the resulting document. The checklist below combines useful procurement details with tax-invoice checks; not every procurement field is a statutory requirement.

### Supplier and customer details

Check the supplier’s legal name and address. For a UAE tax invoice, check the supplier’s tax registration number, commonly called a TRN, and the other required tax-invoice particulars.

A UAE TRN has **15 digits**. Its presence is a useful document check, but it does not by itself establish that every detail is correct or that your business can recover the VAT.

Provide your company’s legal name, billing address and TRN where applicable. Use the details supplied by finance rather than copying a trading name from an email signature.

### Invoice identification and dates

Ask for a clearly identifiable invoice reference, the issue date and a description that connects the charge to your event. The service date is also useful for matching the invoice to the booking and your internal accounting period.

Do not ask the supplier to change a date simply to fit an expense deadline. If a document needs correction, explain the actual error and request the appropriate corrected document.

### A recognisable service description

Ask for enough detail to identify what was purchased. A description such as catering for a named business event, with the service date and location, is easier to reconcile than an unexplained total.

Where relevant, request separate descriptions for food, delivery, service staff, equipment and other agreed services. These are items to clarify with the supplier, not assumed inclusions in every catering booking.

### References required by your company

Tell the caterer whether your organisation requires a purchase-order number, cost centre, department, project code or accounts-payable email address. These details support your internal approval process.

An otherwise accurate invoice can still need administrative clarification if finance cannot identify its owner. Nominate a person who can answer questions about the booking and its approved scope.

## How do you arrange the invoice before the event?

Use a short approval sequence that keeps the event brief and payment process connected. The aim is to settle the requirements before someone pays personally or commits the company to a booking.

1. **Check finance requirements.** Establish whether the expense needs a purchase order, supplier registration, advance approval or a particular invoice format.
2. **Send billing details.** Provide the legal entity, billing address, relevant tax information and invoice recipient.
3. **Confirm service scope.** Agree the event date, location, guest count, menu, dietary requirements and service format.
4. **Approve the paperwork.** Check the quotation, payment request and invoice arrangements against finance instructions.
5. **Reconcile final documents.** Match the final charge and payment evidence to the approved booking, including documented changes.


![Five stages for arranging corporate catering paperwork, from finance checks to final reconciliation](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/e53ca3c9-56ed-4159-8bcd-757c2c69d4ed/body-d384ec5ac448b47584cb0196e327da7a.jpg)

*Agree billing requirements before approving the booking.*


Keep the agreed brief with the invoice rather than relying on separate messages held by different colleagues. If the menu or guest count changes, retain the written approval for the revised scope as well.

For a shared workplace, identify who orders the food and which company receives the invoice. The guide to [catering for co-working spaces in Dubai](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/catering-for-co-working-spaces-in-dubai-complete-guide) addresses the related event-planning context.

## Why do invoice requirements vary?

The right paperwork depends on how your organisation buys the service and what the catering is for. Use these factors to brief the supplier, not as assumptions about its policies.

- **Billing entity:** A company purchase needs the correct business details, even when an individual arranges the event.
- **Payment route:** Employee reimbursement and direct supplier payment require different internal checks.
- **Tax status:** A supplier’s VAT registration status affects whether it can issue a UAE VAT tax invoice.
- **Event purpose:** Staff refreshments, client hospitality and other uses require separate consideration when assessing VAT recovery.
- **Service scope:** Food delivery, staffed service and equipment arrangements need descriptions that reflect what you actually approved.
- **Procurement controls:** Your employer can require purchase-order references, supplier checks or supporting approvals in addition to the invoice.

**Send the finance checklist with the catering brief.** That gives the supplier a chance to confirm what it can provide before you choose a menu or authorise payment.

## Can your company recover VAT on corporate catering?

A valid tax invoice does not automatically make catering VAT recoverable. The UAE Federal Tax Authority’s guidance on input tax and entertainment expenses distinguishes the documentation supporting a purchase from the rules governing recovery.

The UAE’s standard VAT rate is **5%**. Do not apply that figure yourself to an unclear document or assume every supplier must charge VAT; ask the supplier to clarify its tax treatment and have finance check it.

Under the UAE VAT rules, input tax on entertainment provided to customers, potential customers, officials or shareholders is generally blocked. Employee-related food and hospitality also need assessment against the applicable rules and exceptions; calling an event a business meeting does not settle the question.

Give your accountant the event purpose, who attended, the service description and the relevant documents. Avoid deciding recoverability solely from the invoice heading or from the fact that the company paid.

**Expense approval, accounting treatment and VAT recovery are separate decisions.** A supplier can describe its charge, but your finance team must determine how the business records and treats the expense.

## What should the invoice say about staffing and other services?

The invoice should reflect the agreed booking, not leave you guessing about what the total covered. Before approval, ask the supplier to distinguish the food service from any separately agreed operational items.

Check these points against the quotation:

- Whether the booking includes delivery, setup or collection.
- Whether chefs, serving staff or other personnel are part of the agreed scope.
- Whether crockery, glassware, linen or equipment is included or separately arranged.
- Whether drinks, dietary adaptations or additional service requests affect the scope.
- How approved changes after the initial confirmation will be documented.

For myCHEF enquiries, describe the corporate event and ask for the proposed inclusions and exclusions in writing. The supplied brand information confirms corporate event catering, but individual staffing and equipment arrangements need confirmation for your booking.

If you are deciding between food delivery and a staffed event, read about [serving staff and cleanup arrangements](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/can-catering-companies-in-dubai-provide-serving-staff-and-cleanup). Then make sure your chosen scope appears consistently in the quotation and final paperwork.

## Can you claim catering if you paid personally?

Personal payment does not guarantee reimbursement. Your employer’s expense policy determines whether the purchase was authorised and which supporting documents you must submit.

Before paying, ask whether the supplier should bill the company directly or issue the invoice using another approved arrangement. Keep the payment confirmation alongside the invoice, and record the business purpose without including unnecessary personal information about guests.

Do not assume a bank transaction screenshot is enough. It can help show payment, but it does not necessarily explain the catering supplied, the billed entity or the applicable tax details.

## What if the invoice is wrong or only a receipt arrives?

Ask the supplier for the correct document and identify the issue precisely. State whether you need missing company details, a clearer service description, a purchase-order reference or clarification of the tax information.

Keep the original document and the correspondence explaining the correction. Let the supplier issue any replacement or adjustment through its own accounting process; do not edit a supplier invoice yourself.

If a receipt is all you have, ask finance what additional evidence is needed. Then request that evidence from the supplier rather than relabelling the receipt as an invoice.

## FAQ


**Can I get a corporate catering invoice in Dubai in my company’s name?**

Ask the caterer to confirm company invoicing before booking and provide your legal entity name and billing details. Add your TRN where applicable and any purchase-order reference required by finance.

**Is a catering receipt enough for an expense claim?**

A catering receipt is enough only if your employer’s expense policy accepts it for that purchase. Finance can require an invoice, payment evidence and approval records as well.

**Does a corporate catering invoice guarantee VAT recovery?**

A corporate catering invoice does not guarantee VAT recovery. Your finance team must assess the expense purpose and the applicable UAE input-tax rules, including restrictions on entertainment expenses.

**What is the difference between a pro forma invoice and a tax invoice?**

A pro forma invoice requests payment against proposed arrangements; it is not a tax invoice. Ask the supplier which final document it will issue and confirm that it meets your finance team’s requirements.

**Should the caterer include our purchase-order number?**

Ask the caterer to include your purchase-order number if your organisation requires it. Supply the reference before the invoice is prepared and check that it matches the approved booking.

**Can an invoice include food, serving staff and equipment?**

An invoice can describe food, serving staff and equipment when those items form part of the agreed service. Request clear descriptions and confirm which items are included, excluded or separately arranged.

**What should I send when requesting a corporate catering quote?**

Send the event date, Dubai location, guest count, service format and dietary requirements. Include the billing entity, invoice recipient and procurement requirements so the supplier can address the event and paperwork together.


## Settle the billing details with the event brief

The useful final check is simple: can a colleague who did not organise the event match the invoice to the approved booking? Keep the event reference, scope, billing entity and payment evidence connected.

For a myCHEF corporate catering enquiry, send the **date, location, guest count and service required**, together with your company billing details. Ask for written confirmation of the proposed scope and invoice arrangements before you approve the booking.
